title: Inference reliability 90-day cadence & stakeholder canvass
body:
Purpose and context:
We need a focused 90-day experimental cadence to validate SLOs, gating, and rapid rollback patterns for LLM inference surfaces (hosted API + dedicated pools). This doc captures sprint-level hypotheses, milestones, owners, and the stakeholder canvass for cross-team coordination.

High-level hypothesis:
- If we run 3 converging experiments (telemetry fidelity, canary fallback, and cost-aware batching) against a constrained subset of production traffic, we can reduce p99 latency regressions and incident frequency for inference by 25% while keeping unit cost neutral.

Goals (90d):
- Define and adopt 2 primary SLOs for inference: availability (successful-response rate) and tail latency (p99 95th-ile objective).
- Deploy a canary + automated fallback flow for model variants across hosted/dedicated.
- Improve telemetry for KV cache hit/miss and batching efficiency to enable diagnosis within 5 minutes.
- Run three 2-week experiments that produce go/no-go signals for wider rollout.

Proposed SLOs (draft):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful-response rate (5xx / hard timeouts counted) per region, per 7d window.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 450ms for short-seq (<=128 tokens) paths, p99 <= 1200ms for long-seq (>512 tokens) paths, measured per model-class and per instance-type.
- Error budget policy: 7d rolling; automated mitigations when error budget burn rate > 2x.

Success metrics (experiment-level):
- Reduce incident-triggered rollbacks by 25% vs baseline (last 90d).
- Provide mean time to detect (MTTD) for inference degradations <= 3 minutes using new telemetry.
- Canary bake time reduced to <= 30 minutes for basic traffic profiles.

Scope / out-of-scope:
- In scope: hosted API and Redwood Dedicated serving paths, telemetry, canary automation, oncall playbooks, and minimal perf regression tests.
- Out of scope: full Private on-prem packaging, billing/price-model changes, major model architecture changes.

Stakeholder canvass (who needs to be involved):
- SRE (lead): Priya Kumar — cadence, runbooks, incident postmortems.
- Serving runtime: Diego Alvarez — integration points for canary routing and KV cache metrics.
- Observability: Maya Green — dashboard definitions, alert thresholds, tracing hooks.
- Platform engineering: Liam Chen — capacity reservations for canary/dedicated pools, autoscaler knobs.
- Product-hosted-api: Sara Novak — API surface gating, client feature flags, customer communications.
- Solutions/SE: rotational support for customer impact evaluation.

90-day cadence (week-by-week sketch):
- Weeks 0-2 (Prep): finalize SLO definitions, instrument missing metrics (KV cache, batching stats, model-variant tags), create canary routing RFC.
- Weeks 3-4 (Pilot 1: telemetry & alerting): enable high-card telemetry for one model + one region; validate dashboards and alert noise.
- Weeks 5-6 (Pilot 2: canary routing + fallback): deploy canary path for small % of traffic with automated rollback to fallback model variant on error budget burn.
- Weeks 7-8 (Pilot 3: batching/cost experiment): tune batching window & eager commit heuristics for latency-sensitive routes; measure cost delta.
- Weeks 9-12 (Synthesis & rollouts): synthesize experiment outputs, run a controlled broader canary across additional regions, finalize runbooks and SLA update proposal.

Key milestones and deliverables:
- Week 2: SLO definitions documented (Confluence) + dashboards v0.
- Week 4: Telemetry pilot signoff (obs + alerting playbook).
- Week 6: Canary routing RFC and automated rollback workflow in staging.
- Week 8: Cost/batching tradeoff report (baseline vs tuned).
- Week 12: Runbooks, playbooks, and a go/no-go decision for 50% broader rollout.

Operational play patterns (practical):
- Canary routing: implement weighted routing keyed by account/route tag; use feature flagging to move traffic. Canary must include active synthetic probes.
- Automated fallback: when canary error budget burn exceeds threshold or p99 latency regression > 2x baseline, trigger an automated reroute to a compatible variant + alert page oncall.
- Prefix/KV cache validation: add periodic KV cache consistency checks and a "cache-heat" metric to track cold-start impact.

Telemetry and dashboards (must haves):
- Per-model-class: req/s, success rate, p50/p90/p99 latency, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batching_efficiency (tokens/req).
- Error budget burn rate: 1h and 6h windows.
- Canary health board: fraction of canary traffic, synthetic probe latency, rollback count.
- Cost signal: GPU-hours per 1k tokens + ratio before/after batching tuning.

Escalation & runbooks (quick outline):
- Level 0 (alerts): Observability fires page when canary p99 > threshold or success rate < SLO.
- Level 1 (SRE triage): Owner assesses model/infra, checks KV cache heat, checks batching metrics. If clear regression, execute rollback play (automated or manual).
- Post-incident: capture decision log, customer impact, and experiment artifacts.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Serving runtime must expose KV cache and batching instrumentation (ticket ENGINF-342).
- Platform needs ephemeral capacity for canary pools (coord with Liam).
- Observability needs retention policy update to keep high-cardinality metrics for 30d for root-cause.

Risks and mitigations:
- Alert noise causing flapping: mitigate with tuned burn-rate windows and alert aggregation in the canary board.
- Cost regressions from aggressive telemetry: sample metrics where possible and add chargeback tag experiment.
- Customer impact from mis-rolled canaries: enforce synthetic checks + kill switch + two-person approval for >1% traffic.

Experiment templates (each pilot follows this):
- Hypothesis: short one-liner.
- Measurement windows: baseline (7d), trial (7d), cooldown (3d).
- Owner, rollback criteria, expected delta, acceptance criteria.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Finalize precise latency buckets for mixed-token workloads (who owns measurement? obs team).
- Decide account-level vs route-level canaries for minimal blast radius.
- Confirm cost-accounting labels for batching experiments (billing tags).

Meeting cadence & artifacts:
- Weekly sync: Tue 10:00 (30m) owners only — experiment status and blockers.
- Biweekly stakeholder review: Thu 40m — leadership update, roll/no-roll decisions.
- Postmortem/case study: doc within 48h of any production-impacting event.

Immediate action items (first 2 weeks):
- Priya: draft SLO page + share with stakeholders by EOP Week 1.
- Diego: add KV cache and batching metrics to obs ingestion pipeline ticket by Day 3.
- Maya: create dashboard skeleton and wire up synthetic probes by Week 2.
- Liam: provision ephemeral canary pools and reserve minimal 2x headroom by Week 2.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep experiment scope small. Don’t try to tune every model at once.
- Capture failures as learning artifacts — add a short template to Confluence for quick examples.
- Coordinate with CS early if we plan any customer-facing canaries.

References and links:
- Observability draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Inference+Telemetry+Draft
- Serving runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/1289
- Ticket for instrumentation: ENGINF-342

Appendix (short glossary):
- Canary: a limited traffic path to a new model variant or infra config.
- KV cache heat: ratio of warmed cache entries vs total; proxy for cold-start latency impact.

-- end of draft --

Feedback welcome — will iterate after the first sync with serving-runtime and obs.
